claims.summary: The Ministry dictionary defines 零聲母 as a Chinese-character syllable with no consonant and a vowel beginning; it gives 餓, 愛, and 恩 as examples.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 零聲母 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: Official definition and examples 餓、愛、恩.

claims.summary: The NTU phonetics handout discusses Taiwan Mandarin 一 as /∅i/, [ʔi], or [ji], distinguishing phonological zero initial analysis from phonetic onset realizations.

sourceLinks.notes: Course notes present analyses /∅i/, [ʔi], and [ji] and explicitly describe the former as zero-initial.

claims.summary: 愛 and 餓 are official zero-initial examples; the NTU handout discusses the phonological/phonetic analysis of 一.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 零聲母 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: Official dictionary lists 愛 and 餓 among zero-initial syllables.
Official dictionary confirms the reading yī for 一.

claims.summary: Zero initial is a phonological category; the handout’s discussion of 一 does not establish one pronunciation for all Taiwanese speakers.

sourceLinks.notes: The handout reports class/instructor observations and alternatives, not a population-wide sample; the article states this limitation.

semanticReview.method: Manual review of each substantial statement against cited primary institutional source records

findings.supports: Manual comparison with the MOE definition and examples of 零聲母, plus the cited NTU course handout passage on phonological and phonetic analyses of 一; broad orthographic and population-wide assertions were removed.

limitations: The NTU source is dated course material with pedagogical observations rather than a representative acoustic survey; the article explicitly limits its scope.
